title: 2020 AMC 12B Problem 14
statement: Bela and Jenn play the following game on the closed interval \([0, n]\) of the real number line, where \(n\) is a fixed integer greater than \(4.\) They take turns playing, with Bela going first. At his first turn, Bela chooses any real number in the interval \([0, n].\) Thereafter, the player whose turn it is chooses a real number that is more than one unit away from all numbers previously chosen by either player. A player unable to choose such a number loses. Using optimal strategy, which player will win the game?

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: Bela will win if and only if \(n\) is odd.

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: Jenn will win if and only if \(n\) is odd.

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: Jenn will win if and only if \(n \gt 8.\)

solutions.text:
Bela first plays the midpoint \(\tfrac{n}{2}.\) This choice makes the configuration symmetric about the center of the interval.

Thereafter, whenever Jenn picks a number \(x,\) Bela responds with its mirror image \(n - x.\) Since Bela has already chosen \(\tfrac n2,\) Jenn’s legal move satisfies \(\left|x-\tfrac n2\right|>1.\) Therefore \(|x-(n-x)|=2\left|x-\tfrac n2\right|>2,\) so Bela’s response is far enough from Jenn’s new point. Symmetry shows that it is also far enough from every earlier point. Thus Bela always has a move whenever Jenn does, so Jenn is the first to be stuck. Bela always wins.

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Consider what happens if Bela plays exactly at the midpoint of the interval first
After claiming the center, Bela can mirror each of Jenn’s moves through the midpoint
